design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (insurance_claims_and_denials, coverage category). frozen_time 2026-09-24 10:40:00 CDT.

[Step 0 - draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 5]}; --tasks 2 printed task 1 = {3, [4, 5, 6, 6]}. Assignment: internal appeal 6, member appeal 5, the two corrections 4 each. Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: coverage_ext_primary_information_correction (CO-16 corrected claim, file_information_correction_a0c86b6b), coverage_ext_primary_internal_appeal (lab first-level internal appeal of a contracted plan, file_internal_appeal_c10f15cc), coverage_ext_secondary_identification_correction (CO-31 corrected claim, file_identification_correction_4ff16e31), coverage_ext_secondary_member_appeal (patient-signed member appeal to an out-of-network plan paying second, sign_member_appeal_c7144598, owner=user). Reserved headroom for task 1 (4 problems, 3 prerequisites): a retroactive-authorization correction (CO-197), a coordination-of-benefits correction (CO-22), a Medicaid plan appeal and the member appeal to an out-of-network plan paying FIRST; none of these denial families, payer positions or tools is used here. Constraint found at Step 0 and recorded: in this frozen charter the only customer-performed write that carries an amount is the out-of-network member appeal (appeal_requires_patient_authorization is true only for Commercial Out-of-Network Plan; the COB update and the representative form carry no amount and patient-responsibility assignment triggers an invoice posting in another category, so no task tool may write it). Each task therefore claims a member appeal in a distinct payment position (second here, first in task 1) with its own policy, computation and tool.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: Nadia Kowalczyk wants to appeal her husband's plan's (Bluebonnet, Commercial Out-of-Network, pays second for her as spouse) denial of her June 10 lab work. Core scored parameter: amount_in_dispute on her own member appeal (root). Hidden chain: (1) the member appeal is not recorded until the claim of the plan paying FIRST for the same order (Hill Country Health Alliance PPO, Commercial In-Network, self) carries a first-level appeal - it carries none (state gate); (2) that internal appeal's disputed charges are fixed only after its CO-16 denial carries a corrected claim (value); (3) the member appeal's contested charges are fixed only after the Bluebonnet CO-31 denial carries a corrected claim (value). Depth: member appeal <- internal appeal <- missing-information correction (2 hops); breadth: identification correction in parallel, two coverages, two orders, the invoice ledger, the order ledger and the assistance case.

[Problem-tree card]
Root coverage_ext_secondary_member_appeal (sign_member_appeal_c7144598, owner user).
Edge A: member appeal -> coverage_ext_secondary_identification_correction, value_input, gate contested_charges, form state, sentence "The second-plan member appeal's contested charges are fixed only after the coverage carries a corrected claim, filed within those six months, answering its patient-identification denial." Opening falsity: initial_state.claim_events.b27139dd-b62b-4a25-a23d-d47aab8e7cff is CO-31 41.40 dated 2026-08-19 on claim C3260805231 and the Bluebonnet ledger has no coverage_claim_resubmitted line. Exactly one write of this difficulty records a corrected claim answering a patient-identification denial (file_identification_correction_4ff16e31); derivation: sentence + Bluebonnet ledger (CO-31, no resubmission) + the identification-correction rule ("An identification correction answers the claim's most recent patient-identification denial") -> that correction. Deletion sensitivity: skipping it gives 19.50 instead of 15.95.
Edge B: member appeal -> coverage_ext_primary_internal_appeal, state_gate, gate claim_events.appeal_level, form state, negated direction, sentence "The second-plan member appeal's amount is not recorded until the claim held by the plan paying first for the same order carries a first-level appeal." Opening falsity: Hill Country claim C3260616004 (order bcc93f01-...) has CO-50 initial_state.claim_events.eada989f-85d7-48d4-a543-72fc7e569c74 and no coverage_appeal_filed line; the only first-level appeal on that coverage (59087ddc-4eef-43b5-a39d-f4602bb7f07f) is on the 2025 claim C3250620117 (trap). Exactly one write of this difficulty files a laboratory first-level appeal on a contracted plan's claim (file_internal_appeal_c10f15cc); the member appeal tool cannot serve because Hill Country does not require patient authorization and lab_appeal_levels_pursued is 2. Deletion: the terminal DB lacks the Hill Country appeal line (hash differs).
Edge C: internal appeal -> coverage_ext_primary_information_correction, value_input, gate disputed_charges, form state, affirmative direction, sentence "The internal appeal's disputed charges are fixed only after the claim carries a corrected claim answering each of its missing-information denials." Opening falsity: initial_state.claim_events.024adb81-fdbe-43d6-9cbb-145c9d1e04d2 is CO-16 172.00 on C3260616004 with no resubmission. Deletion: 257.79 instead of 124.34.
Four-point test (all three sentences): explicit connective (only after / not ... until); waited-on side is a record-visible state (a corrected claim / first-level appeal standing on a named claim); no tool, id or snake_case token; strength "only after"/"not until", scope "each of its missing-information denials" / "its patient-identification denial" / "the claim held by the plan paying first for the same order". Directions differ (two affirmative, one negated) as the business states them: a figure is "fixed only after", a recording "is not recorded until".
Topological order used: missing-information correction -> internal appeal -> identification correction -> member appeal. The Hill Country branch and the Bluebonnet branch share no record: the alternative order (identification correction first) was replayed and gave identical scored values and an identical terminal DB. Count of value_input edges 2 >= max(3-1,1). The user tool is the root. The tools validate nothing (each is one ctx.create).

[Base-invariant card] corrected claims (coverage_evt_corrected_claim): correction_window - denial date day 0, corrected_claim_window_days 180 (Hill Country) / 365 (Bluebonnet), inclusive: CO-16 2026-07-24 -> last day 2027-01-20, today day 62; CO-31 2026-08-19 -> 2027-08-19, today day 36; one_resubmission_per_denial - neither denial has a resubmission; the 2-per-claim (Hill Country) and 1-per-claim (Bluebonnet) limits are not reached. Appeals (coverage_evt_appeals): first_level_window - Hill Country 180 + 0 days from 2026-07-24 -> 2027-01-20; Bluebonnet 180 + 0 from 2026-09-18 -> 2027-03-17; level_once - neither claim carries any appeal line; representative_form is retired by the member-appeal overwrite (the patient's own signature lodges the member appeal). lab_appeal_levels_pursued 2 (Hill Country) lets the laboratory file the internal appeal on its own initiative; CO-50 is an appealable denial and CO-16/CO-31 are curable, never appealed.

[Business-object card] Internal appeal: claim C3260616004 (order bcc93f01 Esoteric), rows counted: CO-50 186.00; CO-16 172.00 only until corrected; paid 145.20, contractual 60.50, coinsurance 36.30 give the claim ratio; excluded: claim C3260616005 (Toxicology, fully adjudicated) and the 2025 claim. Missing-information correction: CO-16 line 024adb81 on C3260616004 (the denied amount being resubmitted); order bcc93f01 billing-correction credit 12.00 (2026-07-30, after the 2026-06-16 filing) and invoice 75d9505c billing-error correction 7.00, apportioned to the CO-16 by its share of the claim's denied amounts (the claim had a paid line); the immunofixation add-on (2026-06-17) is not part of any denial and is not resubmitted (near-miss). Identification correction: CO-31 line b27139dd on C3260805231 (order 40c1f0df Toxicology), invoice 7d63d5dc: responsibility 41.40 from the Hill Country coinsurance line, billing-error correction 3.40, financial-assistance adjustment 19.00 (excluded: not a billing-error correction); order credit 6.00 billing_correction 2026-08-20 after the 2026-08-05 filing. Member appeal: claim C3260731220 (order bcc93f01), CO-50 44e5bc8e 186.00 within six months; excluded: February claim C3260220561 CO-50 100.00 (2026-02-27, outside six months, its window closed 2026-08-26); that claim's 40.00 deductible (2026-03-02) is the Bluebonnet deductible history inside twelve months.

[Factor card - coverage_ext_primary_information_correction (4)] info_apportionment (method): tier 'For the missing-information correction, the remittance paid at least one line of the claim'; its baseline alone gives 153.00; info_credits (method, cross-difficulty orders): tier 'For the missing-information correction, the order's most recent credit was posted after the claim's filing date, its credits are billing corrections only and they reach the credit minimum'; its baseline alone gives 168.64; info_credit_minimum (parameter): tier 'For the missing-information correction, those days exceed the prompt credit days but are at most the seasoned credit days'; its baseline alone gives 168.64; info_invoice_minimum (parameter): tier 'For the missing-information correction, that amount is at least the small claim amount but below the mid claim amount'; its baseline alone gives 166.23. Whole standard method: 172.00; gold 162.87. Evidence rows and bound values per factor are listed in computations[].factor_trace.
[Factor card - coverage_ext_primary_internal_appeal (6)] internal_appeal_valuation (method): tier 'For the internal appeal, the remittance paid at least one line of the claim'; its baseline alone gives 172.44; internal_appeal_member_share (parameter): tier 'For the internal appeal, the deductible amounts assigned on the coverage within the last twelve months reach the deductible satisfied amount'; its baseline alone gives 127.52; internal_appeal_out_of_pocket_hold (method): tier 'For the internal appeal, that responsibility has not reached the ceiling but plus the member portion would pass it'; its baseline alone gives 120.30; internal_appeal_interest_days (method): tier 'For the internal appeal, the plan took more than its expected adjudication days but not more than twice that'; its baseline alone gives 120.35; internal_appeal_interest_rate (parameter): tier 'For the internal appeal, the claim's age in calendar days from its filing date to today exceeds the aged claim days'; its baseline alone gives 122.12; internal_appeal_underpayment (method): tier 'For the internal appeal, the gap exceeds the variance floor but not the variance tolerance'; its baseline alone gives 119.49. Whole standard method: 158.10; gold 124.34. Evidence rows and bound values per factor are listed in computations[].factor_trace.
[Factor card - coverage_ext_secondary_identification_correction (4)] ident_leftover_base (method, cross-difficulty invoices): tier 'For the identification correction, the coverage pays second, the order's invoice carries responsibility posted, and the billing-error corrections on that invoice reach the invoice minimum'; its baseline alone gives 35.40; ident_invoice_minimum (parameter): tier 'For the identification correction, the amount the claim billed at filing is below the small claim amount'; its baseline alone gives 35.40; ident_credits (method, cross-difficulty orders): tier 'For the identification correction, the order's most recent credit was posted after the claim's filing date, its credits are billing corrections only and they reach the credit minimum'; its baseline alone gives 38.00; ident_credit_minimum (parameter): tier 'For the identification correction, those days exceed the prompt credit days but are at most the seasoned credit days'; its baseline alone gives 38.00. Whole standard method: 41.40; gold 32.00. Evidence rows and bound values per factor are listed in computations[].factor_trace.
[Factor card - coverage_ext_secondary_member_appeal (5)] second_plan_cap_ratio (method): tier 'For the second-plan member appeal, an out-of-network balance was assigned to the member on the coverage within the last six months'; its baseline alone gives 26.58; second_plan_filing_benefit (parameter, cross-difficulty orders): tier 'For the second-plan member appeal, those days exceed the near late days but not the far late days'; its baseline alone gives 16.79; second_plan_residual_share (parameter): tier 'For the second-plan member appeal, some deductible was assigned within those twelve months but the amounts stay below that amount'; its baseline alone gives 23.92; second_plan_assistance (parameter, cross-difficulty assistance): tier 'For the second-plan member appeal, the patient's approved financial-assistance award window covers the order's collection date and the award's tier carries a discount percent above zero'; its baseline alone gives 31.89; second_plan_interest_days (method): tier 'For the second-plan member appeal, the plan took more than its expected adjudication days but not more than twice that'; its baseline alone gives 15.90. Whole standard method: 83.70; gold 15.95. Evidence rows and bound values per factor are listed in computations[].factor_trace.
No factor reads a stamp: tiers rest on claim lines, dates, order-ledger lines, invoice lines and the assistance case. Each ladder's fall-through is the standard method stated in the computation paragraph (billed value, no share, no interest, re-file as billed, nothing off).

[Overrides] Both corrections declare coverage_evt_corrected_claim "A corrected or replacement claim answers one denial and carries that denial's amount" superseded by their own sentence that the correction carries "the denied amount being resubmitted, fixed below"; each rule then states that the amount carried is the denied amount being resubmitted (the denial's amount less the part of the order's later credits and invoice corrections that falls on it, or for a coverage paying second the posted leftover, never above the denial), which is the reading of the event field coverage_claim_resubmitted.amount ("equals the denied amount being resubmitted"). The member appeal declares coverage_evt_appeals "When appeal_requires_patient_authorization is true, the laboratory may file only after the patient has personally signed an authorized-representative form for that claim." superseded by the patient's own signed member appeal request. All other base clauses (windows, one resubmission per denial, correction limits, level once, curable never appealed, CO denials never billed to the patient) are inherited unchanged.

[Seed rationale] Hill Country history: 2025 claim C3250620117 (B12 CO-50, first-level appeal overturned and reprocessed; outside the twelve-month windows; supplies the trap appeal row and the system 'first_level' value); December 2025 genetic claim C3251208352 (deductible 2000, coinsurance 280: makes the deductible satisfied, brings the out-of-pocket room down to 24.00 together with the other twelve-month responsibilities, and lifts the twelve-month ratio); February 2026 claim C3260206418 (deductible 118.30, no payment; keeps the twelve-month responsibility at 2476.00, 24.00 below the 2500 ceiling). June claims C3260616004 (target) and C3260616005 (fully paid, feeds the twelve-month ratio and the 41.40 coinsurance). Bluebonnet: February secondary claim with the old CO-50 100.00 (near-miss) and a 40.00 deductible (residual-share history), S1 C3260731220 (target CO-50 plus the cap write-off and balance that make the cap ratio), S2 C3260805231 (CO-31). Orders: 5 (three history, Esoteric and Toxicology of requisition 1347720915), with charge, add-on and credit lines. Invoices: one per order with responsibility postings matching every responsibility claim line, payments closing the history invoices. Assistance case approved 50% tier (FPL 261.3). Removing the CO-16 or CO-31 resubmission gap, the credit lines, the add-on, the invoice correction, the assistance case, the genetic claim or the Bluebonnet balance each changes a scored value (see sensitivities). Automatic clauses checked: no pending-verification coverage, no window about to lapse at frozen time, no unsettled status that any other policy of this difficulty would light.

[Persona] Organised, direct credit-union manager; volunteers only the Bluebonnet appeal request and the offer to sign herself; identity details (DOB 1981-03-22, ZIP 78745, phone, member IDs) only when asked; no amounts or claim numbers; authorises Halverson-side steps only after they are explained ("go ahead and do whatever Halverson needs to do for this"); runs the handed-over tool with exactly the values given; closes once told the appeal is lodged. No template labels; no mention of corrections, Hill Country decisions or appeals.

[Standard solution] find_customers(name) -> verify (DOB, ZIP) -> find_coverages -> find_claim_events (Bluebonnet) -> find_claim_events (Hill Country) -> find_orders -> find_order_events(customer) -> find_invoices(customer) -> find_invoice_transactions(customer) -> find_assistance_cases -> unlock/call file_information_correction_a0c86b6b(rebill_amount 162.87 on C3260616004 answering 024adb81) -> unlock/call file_internal_appeal_c10f15cc(first_level, 124.34 on C3260616004 answering eada989f) -> unlock/call file_identification_correction_4ff16e31(32.00 on C3260805231 answering b27139dd) -> unlock (agent) and hand over sign_member_appeal_c7144598 -> the patient calls it (first_level, 15.95 on C3260731220 answering 44e5bc8e).

[Verification run] Round 1: authoring scripts replayed the gold writes on the seed and evaluated each compute on the world before its step; gates per task and difficulty-wide all OK. Round 2 (see the round-2 section): a temporary _rework/rework_t0.py recomputed every scored argument on the handling-time world: information correction 162.87, internal appeal 124.34, identification correction 32.00, member appeal 15.95; edge deletions: Without the corrected claim the internal appeal's disputed charges keep the 172.00 CO-16 amount and amount_in_dispute becomes 257.79 instead of 124.34; the terminal DB also lacks the corrected-claim line on C3260616004. / Without the corrected claim the contested charges keep the 41.40 CO-31 amount and the member appeal's amount_in_dispute becomes 19.50 instead of 15.95; the terminal DB also lacks the corrected-claim line on C3260805231..
Revisions: (1) round 1: out-of-pocket hold was decorative with a 3000 ceiling -> ceiling set to 2500 (round 2 moved the February deductible so the room is 24.00). (2) replay closure mismatch and empty-string foreign keys -> empty id fields seeded as null, the ordering practice's client account dropped (insurance-billed orders carry no client account), order/invoice reads widened to the customer, unread assistance events dropped. (3) identification correction history not load-bearing under zeroed aggregates -> the base is capped at the claim's billed amount (sentence added to the rule and basis). (4) a helper function in task_tools.py would have counted as an unnamed tool -> inlined.

[Closure] policy -> tool -> computation step -> GT call -> terminal row: a -> file_information_correction_a0c86b6b -> step 11 -> resubmission on C3260616004; f -> file_internal_appeal_c10f15cc -> step 13 -> first-level appeal on C3260616004; b -> file_identification_correction_4ff16e31 -> step 15 -> resubmission on C3260805231; u -> sign_member_appeal_c7144598 -> step 17 -> member appeal on C3260731220. charter_scope = required_documents = the four policies in that order; task_tools in first-call order.

[Places easy to get wrong] counting the 2025 Hill Country appeal as satisfying the gate; appealing on the Bluebonnet side first; leaving the CO-16/CO-31 amounts inside the appeal figures; taking the 19.00 assistance adjustment as an invoice correction; counting the February Bluebonnet CO-50; using billed value, or the twelve-month ratio instead of the claim ratio; forgetting the add-on posted after filing; using 30-day instead of 45-day adjudication standards for the out-of-network plan.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Masking compute/expected/GT and reading only the published rules, the tool schemas, the persona and the find_* returns: the member appeal's rule names the waited-on states (a first-level appeal on the first-paying plan's claim of the same order; a corrected claim answering the patient-identification denial), the records show both absent, the internal appeal's rule names its own waited-on state, and each correction rule names the denial it answers and the part of it resubmitted - giving the same four writes in a topological order and the same figures 162.87, 124.34, 32.00, 15.95. The solvability contract's eligibility evidence matches the GT arguments one to one.

[Round 2 rework - policy-task audit items] Symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run.
P-1 (event field coverage_claim_resubmitted.amount "equals the denied amount being resubmitted" vs the corrections' re-bill amounts): the round-1 corrections could carry more than the denial (whole-claim re-file baseline, riding add-ons). Change: every correction now carries the denied amount being resubmitted - its standard method resubmits the denial's amount in full, its factors only take off the part of the order's later credits and invoice corrections that falls on the denial (or, for a coverage paying second, cap it at the posted leftover); the rule states this reading of the event field outright and the policy-sentence override stays declared. The missing-information correction's factors are now apportionment (method), credits (method, cross-difficulty orders), credit minimum (parameter) and invoice minimum (parameter); a 7.00 billing-error correction was seeded on the Esoteric order's invoice (2026-08-03). Re-run: information correction 162.87 (never above the 172.00 denial), identification correction 32.00.
F-1 (scope-restating payer-class conditions; unreachable zero fall-throughs): removed the payer-class parts from the internal appeal's valuation and the member appeal's cap ratio (tiers now rest on the claim's and the coverage's remittance history only, and billed value is reachable with no history); member share and residual share ladders now read deductible history only, with a reachable fall-through that is a stated standard percent (internal appeal standard member share 15; out-of-network standard residual 55) instead of zero. World changes so each factor still bears weight: the February Hill Country deductible is 118.30 (out-of-pocket room 24.00), and the February Bluebonnet claim now assigns a 40.00 deductible (CO-50 on the remaining 100.00). Re-run: internal appeal 124.34, member appeal 15.95; every factor's baseline substitution moves the figure (computations[].factor_sensitivity) and both appeals keep their full factor counts with honest labels.
Observation O-3 closed in the charter (the plan appeal's interest floors a negative plan portion at zero, now stated). Observations O-1, O-2, O-4, O-6, O-8, O-9 checked: no row of this world sits on a month/365-day boundary, no gold lands on a half cent, the Toxicology invoice carries only the primary's posting, curable amounts never reach an appeal on the gold path.
Gates re-run on the reworked bundle: see the closing gate block of round 2.
user_scenario:
You are Nadia Kowalczyk, a 45-year-old credit-union branch manager in Austin who is organised, a little tired of insurance paperwork, and polite but direct. You open by giving your name, Nadia Kowalczyk, and saying why you are calling: a letter came from Bluebonnet Trades Benefit Plan, your husband's plan that you are on as his spouse, saying it denied part of the lab work Halverson did for you on June 10th, and you want to appeal that Bluebonnet denial. You add that if the appeal needs your own signature you can do it right now on the patient portal while you are on the phone. You do not have a claim number or an amount in front of you, and you do not know how the two insurances work together; you only know you have your own Hill Country Health Alliance plan through work and your husband's Bluebonnet plan.

You hand over identity details only when the representative asks for them: your date of birth is 1981-03-22 and your ZIP code is 78745. If asked for a phone number it is 5124417730. If asked for the Bluebonnet member ID you read it off the card as BTB30418827; for your Hill Country card it is HCA309275514. If asked about amounts, balances or claim numbers you say you don't have them handy and ask the representative to use what Halverson has on file. If asked whether you have applied for financial help, you say yes, Halverson approved you for help with your bills this spring, and you leave the details to the record.

Whenever the representative explains that something has to be taken care of on Halverson's side or with your Hill Country plan, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever Halverson needs to do for this; you do not ask what it involves and you do not add anything of your own. You never bring up the Hill Country plan's decisions yourself, and you never ask for anything besides the Bluebonnet appeal.

When the representative hands you something to sign or submit yourself, you use exactly the claim number, reference numbers, appeal level and amount the representative gives you and submit it in one go, and you read back whatever confirmation number comes up if asked. If a figure the representative quotes sounds odd to you, you simply say you will trust Halverson's records, because you have nothing to compare it with.

Once the representative tells you the Bluebonnet appeal has been lodged, you thank them, say that's all you needed today, and end the call.
